title: Microfare Snapshot Panel — per-token breakdown, attribution, and export flows
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and prototype a compact 'Microfare Snapshot' panel for Redwood Console that surfaces token-level cost breakdowns, prompt-fragment attribution, and one-click export flows. The panel should be embeddable in route-level dashboards, rollouts views, and the evaluation suite. Primary goals: provide immediate runtime-cost visibility for engineers and product owners, enable fast drilldown to the generating prompt fragments and model variants, and support CSV/Parquet export with role-aware column scrubbing.
acceptance_criteria: Snapshot panel renders per-invocation token counts and cost line items (input tokens, output tokens, KV cache savings, batching delta)
Attribution view maps tokens to prompt fragments or system messages and highlights model variant used; users can toggle attribution by 'prompt fragment' or 'response span'
Export flow supports CSV and Parquet; export options include time range, route filter, and redaction level (none, remove PII, pseudonymize)
Panel respects RBAC: engineers see raw token IDs for debugging; product viewers see aggregated labels and totals only
Panel is responsive and fits into existing route cards in Console without increasing page load time above SLOs (initial sketch validated by Eng)
comments: 2025-02-16 — Aisha Patel: Initial exploratory sketches created, focused on three modes: compact (summary), expand (attribution), export. Shared Figma with stakeholders.

2025-02-18 — Marco Chen (ENG): Reviewed prototype; suggested adding KV cache savings row and a 'batching delta' metric. Raised perf concern about computing fragment attribution on-the-fly for large exports.

2025-02-20 — Priya Singh (PM): Recommended default redaction to 'remove PII' for exported artifacts; add explicit opt-in for raw token export. Wants pricing presets link from the panel for quick scenario simulation.

2025-02-24 — Riley Thompson (RESEARCH): Usability test plan drafted with 6 backend engineers + 4 product managers; primary tasks: identify cost hot-spots, export a 24h slice, trace tokens back to prompts.
2025-02-26 — Aisha Patel: Updated prototype with heatmap sparkline and per-fragment hover state; added export UI with three redaction modes and progress indicator for large exports.
2025-02-28 — Marco Chen (ENG): In review — backend export API PR #8342 linked; noted need for background job for Parquet exports and notification hook in Console.
2025-03-01 — Priya Singh (PM): Design in Review — small UX suggestion to default to aggregated view for non-admins; OK to ship as beta behind feature flag.
notes: Unique aspects: micro-aggregation algorithm to avoid per-token compute at render time, client-side preview for small slices, server-side job for bulk exports. Must coordinate with privacy team for redaction heuristics. Consider exposing a 'pricing presets' CTA that opens Redwood Optimize modal for cost-savings suggestions.
open_questions: What is the retention window for token-level logs exposed in Console?
Should exported Parquet include model variant hashes or only human-readable tags?
Do we implement preview sampling for attribution on large time ranges or require user to narrow window?
design_decisions: Use a three-tier display: Summary row, Inline attribution (expandable), and Full export modal
Default visibility: aggregated totals for viewers, detailed token fragments for roles with 'debug' permission
Export redaction defaults to 'remove PII' but allow explicit admin opt-in to include raw tokens
next_steps: Finalize Figma flows and handoff tokens/variants mapping to Eng (owner: Marco Chen)
Add acceptance tests to Console e2e suite for export job and notification (owner: ENG infra)
Schedule privacy review with Security (owner: Priya Singh)
